title: Lower the CRT key service to literal binary instructions at its caller port
body:
PR #4795 supplied a complete marker-alphabet key service but explicitly left the binary realization of its opaque-payload repair port open. This package compiles and actually executes that entire retained service using one-bit reads/writes, unit bit-head moves and one-bit Boolean/control operations.

For the fixed u2,t2,y8 geometry and targets 0,1,2, a block-simulation proof covers every legal address and supplied target-independent 32-bit ROM. Each source cell has an injective 13-bit encoding for 4,096 opaque payloads plus eight symbols; tagged registers distinguish Booleans from symbols. Each core source instruction lowers to at most 43 actions. Initializing and erasing 492 control bits adds 984 executed actions, giving **141,346,714 binary actions per key** from the retained source bound. Observed counts around 0.9 million are separate evidence, not the proof.

The original `bridge.split` calls the bit executor at its first two actual marked holes using the same physical counter/bad-stream tapes, then continues to the third hole. There is no call-boundary address decoding or key copy inside the executor. The original `one_pass` consumes a projection of the completed returned pairs. The facade still decodes symbols for the unlowered outer controller, and closing the captured prefix is explicit verifier setup; this does not claim a full binary repair layer.

Validation:
- Complete 4,104-symbol codec, 8,208 literal read/dirty-write cases and 172 Boolean/alias cases.
- Four standalone full binary key runs plus two actual caller invocations, totaling 5,348,850 bit/control actions. Independent marker semantics checks all 44,340 source boundaries in the transported parity witness.
- Five faults detected: short bit stride, dirty ROM head, omitted control erasure, dropped Boolean tag and marker collision. Three malformed framed packets reject with physical/control cleanup.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay and source pins pass in about three seconds; a separate read-only review corroborates compiler, proof and actual caller scope.
- Publication-byte/source-history, export integrity and Git-free optimized replay results are recorded below.

Scope remains fixed geometry. Full outer producer/scanner/radix/reinsert control, raw macro-S generation, physical ROM supply, encoded variable-width parameters, uniform compiler costs and total E(p,ell) remain open. No full 2,944-call binary layer, historical suite, new κ or selected-frontier change.

Exact predecessor #4795: `4e4cf7e47f3fc1c40e775d84fb2e7cd2603658cd`, retained unchanged on canonical base `b91956876e5b4122fd89179f1b57557ff8378f15`. The source closure also pins #4752's query program/proof, original #4637 bridge/oracle, scanner increment, compact word and notice. Current #4938 covers evaluator/layout caps, #4942 and reservoir work cover interchange wrappers, #4946 is a census audit, and #4965 studies complex stopped recursion; none supplies this binary key executor.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4709#discussioncomment-19138317

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, preserving all predecessor attribution and source notices; Apache-2.0. No independent human/kernel acceptance claimed. Hosted CI is pending/unverified.

Publication evidence at head `67154122b2867e6dee5b9b25f2f1c862a3e81e95`:
- Three commits separate the literal compiler/proof, independent oracle/caller controls, and reproducible package evidence. Working tree clean; diff whitespace check passes.
- Committed-byte and source-history checks pass for all 17 exported files; canonical base is an ancestor and all nine live inputs are pinned.
- Export integrity passes. Archive SHA-256: `04f1ca0cbf7aa955e2240151c57600c5e3d237d89e8e418ef909e3677d35ea7c`.
- Fresh Git-free export replay with Python `-I -O -W error -B` passes in 2.703 seconds. Independent exported-source drift and frozen-result drift controls both reject.

Final scoped overlap checkpoint: offline search on 2026-10-23 05:16 UTC of `binary lowering`, `binary key`, `crt-paid-key-service`, and `opaque payload` used the complete 323-open-PR snapshot (05:14:01 UTC), 4,077-discussion snapshot (05:14:50 UTC), and 6,638 local notes at the exact submission head. Thirteen hits were the retained predecessors, this claim/package/hub pointer, and unrelated selected-stream work; no matching new executor lead was found. This is a cached prose search, not a novelty proof. A live recheck confirms merged #4795 still has head `4e4cf7e47f3fc1c40e775d84fb2e7cd2603658cd`.
